beats.text: Balogun Market, Saturday. You came for fabric. Behind a shoe stall, shouting prices in pure Benin pidgin: Osaze.
Customer! Original Italian! Oga Osaze, see your babe o!
{tell}

never_left.text: On the stall: rows of his exact loafers. Every insole says 'Made in Aba'.

outcomes.text: Six yards of ankara you don't need. He texts later: 'Back from Milan meetings, bella.' You reply with a thumbs up.

outcomes.text: He sits on a crate. 'I never left. Visa refused three times. Milan was a dream I talked about until I believed it.'

choices.label: Haggle for a pair of his 'Italian' loafers.
choices.receipt: You bought 'Italian' loafers from his stall.

choices.label: Go live: "Euro-returnee spotted in Balogun."
choices.receipt: You livestreamed him at his Balogun stall.

outcomes.text: 18k viewers. Chidi waves, advertising his stall. Osaze's 'Milan' Instagram is deactivated by evening.

choices.label: Walk away. Block him at the bus stop.
choices.receipt: You walked away and blocked him at the bus stop.

outcomes.text: You block him at CMS bus stop. A conductor shouts 'Obalende!' It feels like a sign.

choices.label: "Refund my 'clearing' money. Now."
choices.receipt: You demanded your money back at his stall.

choices.label: "Your mama told me about Ikeja."
choices.receipt: You told him his mother had let it slip.

outcomes.text: He laughs, then he doesn't. 'She always tells.' He looks almost relieved somebody finally knows.

beats.text: He's in the shower. His iPad rings on the bed. Video call: 'Ivie ❤️'. You answer.
Who are you? Where is my husband? Osa, go to your room.
{tell}

wife_abroad.text: Behind her, on the fridge: the crayon house from his lockscreen. Three stick people. One is labelled 'Papà'.

choices.label: Hang up. Say nothing. Ever.
choices.receipt: You hung up on his wife and said nothing.

outcomes.text: You hang up. He comes out humming. You smile. Your smile is a crime scene.

choices.label: Talk to Ivie. Calmly. Honestly.
choices.receipt: You talked to his wife, honestly.

outcomes.text: An hour. Rent in Torino, Osa's school, his 'Lagos business'. You are the Lagos business.

choices.label: Hand him the iPad when he comes out.
choices.receipt: You handed him the iPad with his wife on it.

outcomes.text: He takes it, dripping, caught. Then he sits on the bed and tells you everything. 'It's dead but Italian.' He wants you anyway.

choices.label: Screenshot the call. Post it.
choices.receipt: You posted a screenshot of his wife's video call.

outcomes.text: The Parlour finds Ivie's Facebook in eight minutes. Torino and Lekki are in the same comment section now.

choices.label: Leave the iPad ringing. Leave him.
choices.receipt: You left while his wife was still calling.

outcomes.text: You leave it face up on his pillow, still ringing. Let Europe time handle him.

choices.label: "I've seen Osa before. On your balcony."
choices.receipt: You told him you'd seen his son before.

outcomes.text: He sits down slowly. 'He's six. He's everything.' The first fully honest thing you've heard from him.

choices.label: "Was my 'papers' money her rent?"
choices.receipt: You asked if your 'papers' money paid his wife's rent.

outcomes.text: Ivie answers for him: 'He sent ₦200k last week. That was you? Thank you.' She means it.

choices.label: Send his ₦1.8m straight to Ivie.
choices.receipt: You sent the money you were holding to his wife.

outcomes.text: You transfer it all to Torino with a note: 'From Lagos, with clarity.' Ivie sends a heart. Osaze sends a scream.

beats.text: 9am. He's back from the embassy, holding a brown envelope like it might explode. He sits on your bed.
Visa approved. Milan, a job, a flat. I never told you because I was scared. Come with me.
{tell}

japa_real.text: His jacket still smells of the 5am queue: rain, diesel and other people's hope.

choices.label: "Yes. Show me the plan."
choices.receipt: You said yes to Milan.

outcomes.text: A folder: your CV, schools, a spare key already cut. You cry. He cries. The envelope is damp now.

choices.receipt: You asked to see the visa before saying yes.

outcomes.text: Real visa, real stamp, real job letter. He laughs: 'Investigate me. I deserve it.'

choices.label: "I love you. But my life is in Lagos."

outcomes.text: He holds you a long time. 'Then we do long distance. Or I come back. We'll see.' He means every option.

choices.label: Announce it before he can tell anyone.

choices.label: "So my ₦200k really was papers?"
choices.receipt: You asked if your papers money was real.

outcomes.text: He opens the folder: a receipt in your name. 'Your biometrics are next week.' The papers money was real.

choices.label: Hum 'Volare'. Say yes without words.

outcomes.text: He stops mid-sentence. Then he joins in, badly, loudly, crying. The neighbours knock. Nobody cares.

outcomes.text: He replies: 'Nobody. Lagos people.' Then he's typing for a long time.
